reigns.note: Forefather of the single-line Ithacan house — father of Laertes and grandsire of Odysseus — whose race the suitors sought to wipe from Ithaca; Homer names him as the stem of the high-roofed halls, not a catalogue king with a separate reign narrative.
Once lord of the Cephallenians; in old age withdrew to his country farm while suitors devoured his son's house — the funeral shroud Penelope wove in his name held the wooers at bay.
King of rocky Ithaca and captain of the Cephallenian contingent at Troy.

Sole heir of the house: kingship in sea-girt Ithaca is by birth his heritage. Homer closes before a settled succession after Odysseus' return; later variants remove him from the island with Telegonus rather than enthroning him as a long-reigning king.
